findings.title: Source files exceed the ~300-line guideline
findings.description: The line counts of the three modified cutover scripts are 311 (`cutover_304_checks.py`), 308 (`cutover_304_first_purchase.py`) and 312 (`cutover_304_evidence.py`). These counts come from a grep that includes blank lines. `purchase_verdicts.py` was split out explicitly to stay near 300 lines, but the other three files grew past that mark anyway. Each is only slightly over. The overshoot is minor, and `_check_scope`, `_check_resubmit` and `resubmit_origins` could move into a separate module.

findings.title: Mixed `fetch_status` vocabulary and bucket names are matched by string literals
findings.description: The `_NEEDS_REASON`, `_NEVER_ACCOUNTED`, `_NEEDS_PUBLICATION` and `_LISTED_NEVER` sets are built from `TickSessionStatus` values, so that part is fine. `_unaccounted` falls through to a `CutoverError` for any bucket not in those four sets, so a new status will stop the cutover. That is the intended fail-closed behaviour and is tested. However, the other `purchase_verdicts` literals, such as `ISSUE_CLOSED = "CLOSED"`, depend on `gh` output text. A short comment next to `ISSUE_CLOSED` shows the author considered this. Even so, `_label` compares session dates and request ranges as ISO strings (`request.start <= day < request.end`). That is correct only while the formats match exactly, and `str(date)` does match. Parsing them as `date` objects would make this robust. It is minor.

findings.title: `main` swallows `SystemExit` from argparse
findings.description: `main` catches `SystemExit` around `parse_args` and returns `int(exc.code or 0)`. The inline comment justifies this: argparse has already printed usage, and `main` returns its exit code so the code is testable. It is a narrow, justified swallow. One edge case: `SystemExit.code` can be a string, which would make `int()` raise `ValueError`. argparse only emits ints, so this is theoretical. A simpler design would pass `argv` to a parser configured with `exit_on_error=False`, or let `SystemExit` propagate.

findings.title: Unrecoverable `--estimate` mode relies on a hand-copied state-write guard in tests
findings.description: The test asserts that no install, pass or baseline call happens by monkeypatching `install_release`, `run_passes` and `record_start_and_baselines`. `_estimate_only` also calls `evidence.mt_json` inside `judge` only when `since is not None`, which `--estimate` never triggers. That test therefore confirms the happy path but not that `judge` skips the `debug requests` read for `start=None`. Add a case in which a resubmit exists and `start=None`. It should expect the "is a resubmit" refusal and make no extra `mt_json` call.

findings.title: Ceiling command is now derived instead of hardcoded
findings.description: The old fixed ceilings (7 and 16) are replaced by values rounded up to a $5 step, computed from the estimate. This removes a magic default, and the tests cover the boundary cases (multiples of 5 are not raised). Using `Decimal` with `ROUND_CEILING` and formatting with `:f` avoids exponent notation. The design is sound.

findings.title: Tests build real CLI payloads rather than hand-made shapes
findings.description: The tests construct documents through `accounting_futures._product_payload`, `coverage_to_dict` and `tick_debug_cmds._cell`. This follows the parser-fixture rule in the project guidelines. The `test_bar_job_dirs_read_the_rows_the_real_cli_renders` test directly guards the symbols-shape drift that the latest commit fixed.
